full_judgment:
This Miscellaneous Case arises out of an application under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for transfer of the Family Court Case No. 7 of 1992 pending before the Family Court Judge (Assistant Judge), Pirojpur Sadar transferring the same to any other court of competent jurisdiction within larger Districts of Khulna, Jessore or Kushtia. 

 2. The opposite party as plaintiff filed the aforementioned Family Court case on 14-5-1992 praying for restitution of conjugal right and recovery of the defendant-petitioner as the married wife of the plaintiff on 5-1-1985 through a Kabinnama, the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 were living a happy conjugal life and a daughter was born on 26-5-1988, on 17-9-1990 the mother of the defendant No. 1 took her with gold ornaments to her parental home and since then the defendant did not return to the plaintiff''s house and the plaintiff along with others came to the house of her parents to bring her to his home, the defendant did not refuse to come to his house but her mother disclosed that she will be given in marriage to someone else the defendant created talaknama of the plaintiff on 23-4-1992 so he filed this suit in the Family Court at Pirojpur. After filing the suit the plaintiff moved an application under section 16(A) of the Family Courts Ordinance praying for an injunction restraining re-marriage of the defendant pending the suit. 

 3. Her case, in short, is that the defendant divorced the plaintiff by registered talaknama on 23-4-1992 on the ground that the plaintiff is unemployed, characterless and a debauch, habitual drunkard and associate of persons of similar character, he procures money by unfair means and from his parents for such abnormal and anti-social vicious life and makes the life of the defendant miserable by inhuman and cruel treatment and torture. 

 6. Mr Md Abdur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that in view of the decision of his court that the suit for restitution of conjugal rights is void and nullity because the same is in violation of the fundamental law of the land as incorporated in the Constitution of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh. He submits that the defendant-petitioner also cannot go to Pirojpur to contest the suit by filing written statement and also to file written objection with affidavit necessary for the same as she apprehends bonafide that the plaintiff-opposite party with the help of his bad and characterless associates and the merciless hooligans will forcefully take her into their custody and after torture will kill her. In such circumstances the suit should be transferred to any other court of competent jurisdiction within the districts of Khulna, Jessore or Kushtia for ends of justice. He submits that if the suit is not transferred to any place of the aforementioned Districts then the defendant petitioner will not be able to go to Pirojpur and contest the suit as plaintiff opposite party lives in Pirojpur town. The learned Advocate submits that as per provisions of the Constitution of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh the suit is inoperative as law itself is void and illegal and therefore, the same should be upheld and by an order from this court the Family Law court case No.7 of 1972 be declared void and, as such, the suit cannot continue any longer. In such circumstances the prayer and submissions for transfer of the case under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure will not be required. 

 7. There was no appearance of the plaintiff in this case in spite of the fact that the notice was duly served upon the plaintiff-opposite party of this case. 

 8. I heard the learned Advocate of the petitioner, perused the petition and the relevant papers. The suit for restitution of conjugal rights is in violation of Article 17 of the Constitution of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh and with the promulgation of the Constitution the said provision of law has became void as the same is directly against the provisions of the Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Constitution. In this respect I have delivered two judgments with reference to a case reported in 34 DLR page 221. The constitutional guarantee of equality of man and woman and liberty of the citizen in such circumstances the wife cannot be dragged and compelled by the husband to live with him by a decree of restitution of conjugal rights against her will. Moreover, the decree even if passed cannot be executed and so if the decree is inexecutable then the suit is infructuous. According to the provision of the Code of Civil Procedure, decree could be executed by sending the defendant to the jail for the same but subsequently it was amended in 1923 and the provision was abolished. Thereafter, it can be only executed by attachment of the property of the defendant but in almost all the cases where the suit is restitution of conjugal right against the wife by the husband the decree cannot be executed as in every case wife has got no properties. The marriage is a human relationship between a man and woman and the same exists with the adjustment between the parties and if there is breach in this relationship nothing remains in respect of this peaceful happy relationship. In Muslim law marriage is a social contract between a man and woman in presence of witnesses solemnised by the recitation from the Holy Quaran. So if there is breach of contract of marriage by any party it can be challenged in the court. But if there is a decree in the suit against the person of the defendant be effectively executed. The male partner of the contract of marriage has got arbitrary power of divorce of his female partner just by pronouncing divorce but the female partner of marriage has got no arbitrary power in this respect and therefore subsequent legislation has allowed her right of talak-e-taufiz. That means right of divorce by the female to her male partner in the contract of her marriage and more so she can file suit for dissolution of marriage of the husband on specific grounds as embodied in the Muslim Dissolution of Marriage Act of 1939. In the Constitution of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh the Fundamental Rights under Article 26(2) read with Article 7 declares such law as void, Articles 27, 28, 31 and 32 have been incorporated in the Constitution and so in consideration of those provisions of law of the Constitution it has been decided by this court that the dictum of restitution of conjugal right is a violation of life, liberty, freedom, equality and social justice as guaranteed in the above Articles of the Constitution, so no law can be passed and the existing law which is against the provision of the Constitution must become void. In such circumstances I can safely say and declare that the restitution of conjugal rights either by the husband against his wife or by the wife against her husband is an invalid and void piece of law and so no suits for restitution of conjugal right can continue before the courts as the same are void and illegal. Reference be given in 34 DLR page 221 and Civil Revision No.5195 of 1991 (Dhaka). Judgment dated 4-7-1994. 

 9. In consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the discussions made above, I am of the view that the suit be transferred from the Family Court of Pirojpur to the Family Court of Jhenaidah Sadar and the same be dismissed by that court as not maintainable in view of the observations made by me. 

 In the result I make the Rule absolute and transfer the Family Court case No.7 of 1992 from the Family Court and Assistant Judge of Pirojpur to the Family Court at Jhenaidah Sadar for passing necessary orders dismissing the case as the very foundation of the suit for restitution of conjugal right is void with the promulgation of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. In consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case I pass no order as to cost.
